entry.title: Valuing the Tarot Interviews Catalog
entry.summary: When you build something entirely by hand and without a safety net, you have to remind yourself of the…
entry.content:
When you build something entirely by hand and without a safety net, you have to remind yourself of the project's worth.

I recently sat down to map out the true editorial media value across every single podcast episode and written feature across Tarot Interviews and Tarot DMs.

Across more than 70 generous contributions, I weighed three things: what it would cost to commercially produce this work, the real effort of securing each guest, and the actual reach of the audience that showed up to listen and read.

The archive at a glance

  • Combined Output: £57,226 (conservative range: £31,712 to £95,155)
  • Tarot Interviews: £20,451
  • Tarot DMs: £36,775

This figure represents the raw craft, hours, and distribution effort required to bring this entire archive into the world.

The people who inhabit this space make it so special. Literary powerhouses like Joanne Harris, Adrian Tchaikovsky, and Lauren Beukes share the exact same floor space with underground musicians, visual artists, academics, stage performers, and festival regulars. Tarot DMs carried a massive share of this footprint, with individual features touching anywhere between 4,000 and 60,000 readers.

What we give back to our guests

  • Per Guest Feature: £829 avg in equivalent promotional and editorial value
  • Weekly Output (4 features a week): £3,316
  • Monthly Impact: £14,369
  • Annual Impact: £172,432

Every person who sits down for an interview receives a permanent piece of original media that stays online, alongside the advertising-equivalent weight of its audience reach.

Putting concrete numbers to this work gives us an undeniable baseline for future conversations about funding, sponsorship, and long-term partnerships.

Counting all of this up makes me wonder where the Tarot Interviews project will be next year.

entry.title: Tarot Interviews Joins Podcasting’s 1%
entry.summary: Only 1% of podcasts launched are estimated to reach break-even or better. My Tarot Interviews podcast has now done…
entry.content:
Only 1% of podcasts launched are estimated to reach break-even or better.

My Tarot Interviews podcast has now done that in eighteen months, recovering its original equipment costs.

Now, this does not include my time, but it is still a milestone for an independently produced podcast using an experimental format in a specialist field.

Thank you to everyone who helped it get here!

Take a listen by visiting https://tarotinterviews.com

entry.title: Previous Guests
entry.summary: It is not every day you get to pause and reflect on how far a creative project has come,…
entry.content:
It is not every day you get to pause and reflect on how far a creative project has come, but today is one of those days! 

I recently sat down to update the guest directory for my projects, Tarot Interviews and Tarot DMs, and realized we’ve hit a pretty wonderful milestone: we have officially featured over 70 guests and contributors. For those new to the project, the premise is simple but revealing: a three-card, three-question format used to interview writers, artists, musicians, and cultural figures.

Over the course of 70+ interviews, this format has adapted into two spaces:

  • Tarot Interviews: A traditional audio podcast format.
  • Tarot DMs: Written interviews conducted entirely through messaging apps.

The most rewarding part of this journey has been the sheer diversity of the people who have agreed to sit down (or log on) and pull cards with me. I have spoken with internationally bestselling authors like Joanne Harris and Adrian Tchaikovsky, brilliant narrative designers, historians, and musicians. Tarot Interviews has even taken the format on the road, interviewing festival crew members, artisan blacksmiths, and performers right in the middle of muddy fields!

A huge thank you to all the creative minds who have trusted me with their time and their stories.

If you want to see the full, newly updated list of guests, or check out the format for yourself, you can find the directory over on https://tarotinterviews.com/previous-guests

entry.title: Finbarre at the Tarot Cultures conference
entry.summary: If you want a sign that arts and humanities are still very much in demand in 2026, take a…
entry.content:
If you want a sign that arts and humanities are still very much in demand in 2026, take a look at this room!

This weekend I presented my paper, “Tarot Reading as Living Heritage: Documenting Contemporary Rider-Waite-Smith Practice in the UK,” as part of Tarot Cultures, a conference organised by Goldsmiths, University of London.

The paper drew on my work coordinating the UK living heritage submission for Rider-Waite-Smith tarot reading practice.

The process involved gathering public testimony and documentation from readers, teachers, writers, artists, archivists and tarot communities about how the practice is carried, taught, adapted and understood today.

For the talk, I used the Three of Pentacles as my central image: an unfinished structure, worked on by many hands over time. It felt like a useful way to think about tarot as living heritage - a practice sustained through use and care.

I’m grateful to the organisers, speakers and attendees for such a well organized and generous conference! It was a real privilege to place contemporary tarot practice in conversation with other esoteric research.

entry.title: Welcome
entry.summary: I'm an arts and culture journalist, tarot researcher, producer and creative technologist based in Beeston, Nottinghamshire. I use tarot…
entry.content:
I'm an arts and culture journalist, tarot researcher, producer and creative technologist based in Beeston, Nottinghamshire.

I use tarot and unconventional interview formats to create conversations with artists, writers and musicians, and to explore tarot as a living cultural practice.

My work ranges from Tarot Interviews and Tarot DMs to research, archives and public heritage projects.

A new kind of interview

Since getting my start in broadcasting in 2005, I've seen the same standard Q&As play out again and again. I became interested in what happens when you give up some of that control.

In Tarot Interviews and Tarot DMs, randomly drawn cards provide the starting point, an interview shaped by chance. One structured enough to create a conversation, unpredictable enough to take it somewhere new.

Featured guests

My interview projects have featured creatives across literature, music and the arts, including Joanne Harris, Lauren Beukes, Adrian Tchaikovsky, Julian Simpson, Lucy Rose, C.B. Lee and Sacha Coward.

Explore my projects →

Research & tarot heritage

Alongside my journalism, I research tarot as culture, history and living practice. My work includes the British Tarot Archive, Rider-Waite-Smith research, public heritage projects and research into chance-based interviewing.

Explore my research →

Work with me

I'm available for festival and event coverage, interviews and media appearances, research enquiries, speaking and creative collaborations.
